clue.text: Not a quick examination

parts.note: 'quick' in its old sense means living, so an examination of someone not quick is one carried out on a dead body

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a check-up was slow and thorough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' looks like it means fast, but it is the old word for alive, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: A post-mortem is the examination of a corpse, a person no longer living.

clue.text: A doctor came to pre-eminence as a saint

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's degree
rose means climbed to prominence

explanation.surface: A doctor became famous as a holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: MB is a medical degree, so it stands for a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ambrose was a fourth-century bishop of Milan, venerated by the Church.

clue.text: Drink able to stop wind?

indicators.note: to stop means the word able plugs a gap inside the word for wind

parts.note: to wind thread is to twine it

explanation.surface: Can a beverage cure flatulence?
explanation.walkthrough: 'wind' looks like gas or breeze, but it is the verb, to twist, giving TWINE; 'to stop' plugs ABLE into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary wine served with meals is a beverage.

clue.text: Father and friend of Roman authority

parts.note: pa is a word for father
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A priest and his companion obey the Vatican.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman' points to the Pope in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope's authority is centred on Rome, so anything from him is pontifical.

clue.text: Always giving agreement to right order of drinks

parts.note: yea is a word of agreement
a round is one set of drinks bought for a group

explanation.surface: Someone always agrees it is right to buy the next drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link. A round is a set of drinks one person buys for everyone at a British pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening throughout all seasons happens at all times.

clue.text: Start German after a bit of maths

parts.note: trig, short for trigonometry, is a branch of mathematics

explanation.surface: A German pupil begins his lesson after a little maths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places GER after TRIG in the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: To trigger something is to set it off or cause it to begin.

clue.text: Article about English going to Spain gets a laugh

indicators.note: about means the article is wrapped around English

parts.note: the is the definite article
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about an Englishman moving to Spain is amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside THE, giving TEHE; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tee-hee is a giggle or snigger.

clue.text: Mined at sea, given ludicrously tiny compensation

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of mined are thrown into disorder
ludicrously means absurdly, so the letters of tiny are rearranged

explanation.surface: A ship mined at sea is offered absurdly little in damages.
explanation.walkthrough: Two anagrams: 'at sea' turns MINED into INDEM, and 'ludicrously' turns TINY into NITY. 'given' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An indemnity is a payment made to cover loss or damage.

clue.text: Greek is eating Italian breakfast cereal

indicators.note: eating means the word is swallows the Italian inside it

parts.note: IT is the abbreviation for Italian

explanation.surface: A Greek man is eating an Italian's morning porridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eating' puts IT inside IS. Grits is coarsely ground hominy eaten in the American South.
explanation.definitionFit: Grits is a coarse ground maize porridge eaten at breakfast.

clue.text: Reducing sail hurt finger with end of wire

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so the letters are knocked into a new order
end of picks out the last letter of wire

explanation.surface: A sailor taking in canvas cut his finger on a wire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of' gives E from wire; 'hurt' rearranges FINGER plus E. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reef is to shorten a sail by rolling or folding part of it.

clue.text: Dancing to pop music has to be a hit

parts.note: taken as written, minus the link 'to'
a bop is a blow or punch

explanation.surface: Someone insists that dancing to pop music must be a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' joins definition and wordplay; 'a hit' looks like a chart success, but it is a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: Bebop, or bop, names both a jazz style and the dancing done to popular music.

clue.text: Handy mix sounds correct for mineral

indicators.note: the letters of handy are mixed up into a new order
sounds says the next word is replaced by one pronounced the same

parts.note: correct means right

explanation.surface: A recipe suggests that a convenient blend sounds right for a stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mix' turns HANDY into ANHYD; 'sounds' turns RIGHT into the same-sounding RITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Anhydrite is a calcium sulphate rock-forming substance, a natural crystalline compound.

clue.text: Made too much of Elgar's variation?

definitions.text: Made too much of Elgar's variation?

parts.note: over as a prefix means excessively, as in overdone

indicators.note: a variation is a reworking, so the composer's name is rearranged

parts.note: the composer's name, with the possessive giving no letter

explanation.surface: A critic complains that one of Elgar's Enigma Variations was inflated.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: making too much of a piece swells it beyond due size, while 'variation' rearranges ELGAR into LARGE after OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Something blown up beyond proper size is excessively big, and a variation can inflate its theme.

clue.text: Kenyan mother's first-class

parts.note: ma is mother, with the 's kept as S
A1 means first-class, written as the letters AI

explanation.surface: A Kenyan's mother is top-notch.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate, from shipping registers) is read as the letters AI.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a pastoral people of Kenya and Tanzania, so a member is a Kenyan.

clue.text: Awfully idle European appears to miss out letter!

indicators.note: awfully says the letters of idle are badly jumbled

explanation.surface: A lazy European seems to skip a letter in his writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges IDLE into ELID; 'appears to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To elide is to omit a sound or character when speaking or writing a word.

clue.text: Jump seat fixed to start travelling from Leeds to Hull?

indicators.note: to start places the anagram at the front, before the jump
fixed means repaired or rearranged, so the letters of seat are put in a new order

parts.note: to bound is to jump

explanation.surface: Someone leaps into a newly repaired seat to set off on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' turns SEAT into EAST, and 'to start' puts it before BOUND. Hull lies east of Leeds in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip from Leeds to Hull heads towards the North Sea coast, in the sunrise direction.

clue.text: Fun spoiled, becoming ill, but completely reliable

indicators.note: spoiled says the word fun is ruined into a new order

parts.note: ailing means falling sick

explanation.surface: A party is ruined when someone feels sick, though the host never lets anyone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoiled' rearranges FUN into UNF; 'but' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never lets you down is dependable at all times.

clue.text: Nice smell of paper in European country

indicators.note: in says the paper sits inside the country

parts.note: France is a country in Europe
rag is slang for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A French newspaper has a pleasant whiff about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like 'pleasant', but it is also the French city, which suits the France in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrance is a pleasant scent.

clue.text: Popular with an Ulster friend though not in the least lively

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an means a
NI, Northern Ireland, is Ulster
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A well-liked Northern Irish friend is utterly dull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link. Ulster is used for Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lifeless shows no sign of being alive.

clue.text: Merrily replays CD, whereby time's reduced to a trickle?

definitions.text: whereby time's reduced to a trickle?

indicators.note: merrily says the letters are tossed about gaily into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone happily plays a CD again and again until the hours drain away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Merrily' rearranges REPLAYSCD. The definition describes the device rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A water clock measures time by the steady flow of water out of a vessel.

clue.text: Stick to Cyprus for this sport?

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
to stick is to cling

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker sticks to Cyprus for a pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'for' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Cycling is riding bicycles for exercise or competition.

clue.text: Poet's agreement to accept alternative technology

indicators.note: to accept means the word for agreement takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: yes is a word of agreement
AT is the abbreviation for alternative technology

explanation.surface: A poet agrees to take on green energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poet's' is read as 'Poet is'. 'to accept' puts AT inside YES.
explanation.definitionFit: W. B. Yeats was the Irish writer of 'The Second Coming', so he is a poet.

clue.text: Central American wife?

parts.note: CA is the abbreviation for Central America
Eve was made from Adam's rib, so a wife is called a rib

explanation.surface: A man has married a woman from Central America.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a Carib woman could be a Central American wife, and RIB for wife comes from the Genesis story of Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribs are an indigenous people of the Caribbean coast and Central America.

clue.text: Proportion of allowance cut

indicators.note: cut means the word for allowance loses its last letter

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

explanation.surface: A share of the allowance was reduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes the final N from RATION; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratio is the relation of one quantity to another.

clue.text: Grieving old bishop engaged in broadcasting

indicators.note: engaged in means the old bishop is held within the word for broadcasting

parts.note: broadcasting seed by hand is sowing it
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A mourning former bishop is busy with radio work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcasting' looks like radio, but it is scattering seed. 'engaged in' puts ORR inside SOWING after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mourning feels deep sorrow, so is lamenting a loss.

clue.text: Steps made from tiles

indicators.note: made from says the letters of tiles are used to build a new word

explanation.surface: Some steps were built out of tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made from' rearranges TILES.
explanation.definitionFit: A stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence or wall.

clue.text: Veteran army type

annotationWithheld.why: The clue held for OLDIE is 'Veteran army type': 'Veteran' defines, but no reading of 'army type' gives the rest of the letters, and no other print of the clue was found.

clue.text: One runs in to assembling characters? That's it

definitions.text: One runs in to assembling characters? That's it

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: assembling the letters means putting them together in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone barges in on a group putting letters together.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: running in on others is an intrusion. 'assembling characters' rearranges RUNSINTO after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Barging in where one is not wanted is an unwelcome entry.

clue.text: Admiral Byrd, reportedly?

definitions.meaning: Sir Francis ... was an Elizabethan English admiral
Byrd sounds like bird, and a male duck is one

explanation.surface: A question about the American admiral Richard Byrd.
explanation.walkthrough: Byrd was a real American admiral, which hides the second reading: said out loud, Byrd is a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Drake was a famous naval commander, and a male duck is a kind of waterfowl.

clue.text: Tynesider forced ogre to pass on

indicators.note: forced says the letters of ogre are pushed into a new order

parts.note: to pass on is to die

explanation.surface: A man from Newcastle made a monster die.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' rearranges OGRE into GEOR. The Tyne is the river at Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle and the Tyneside area.

clue.text: Component some of clientele mentioned

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A shop's regulars mentioned a part.
explanation.definitionFit: An element is a basic part of a whole.
